title: Keep history-only PR Snapshots current
summary: Pull request context matching now recognizes a completed Snapshot as current whenever every following commit is eve history only, even when the PR contains earlier feature work before that Snapshot. PR #36 therefore remains linked to its latest Snapshot and appears in the eve review queue. The detail page now surfaces GitHub's actual merge conflict instead of a false stale-review state.
userVisibleChange: PR #36 and other multi-Snapshot eve branches no longer become falsely stale after their required eve history commit. They stay in the eve review queue, and genuine GitHub merge conflicts are named directly.

risks.title: History-only matching depends on first-parent topology
risks.mitigation: The matcher verifies implementation ancestry, the committed Snapshot record, every intervening commit's parent chain, and that each non-merge commit changes only `.eve`; focused regressions cover both history-only acceptance and product-changing merge rejection.

decisions.title: Trust first-parent history-only topology without whole-PR delta comparison
decisions.rationale: When no merge occurs after the Snapshot implementation, ancestry plus a committed Snapshot record and `.eve`-only following commits prove that product code did not change. Comparing the latest Snapshot delta with the whole multi-Snapshot PR delta incorrectly includes earlier feature work.

decisions.title: Keep strict product comparison for target merges
decisions.rationale: A target-branch merge can alter product code through conflict resolution, so normalized product-delta validation remains required whenever a merge follows the Snapshot.

decisions.title: Prioritize a confirmed GitHub conflict after freshness
decisions.rationale: Once Snapshot coverage is current, a known merge conflict is the most actionable blocker and should be named in the badge and side panel while Plan/evidence status remains visible in the readiness grid.
